newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy money market rate cut hopes on hold.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy money market rate cut hopes on hold.

text.p: Italy's money market has put hopes of an early official rate cut on hold for now while further out it is beginning to discount EMU uncertainties, according to a weekly study of implicit rates carried out by the Bocconi University's research arm Igier for Reuters.

The study showed the market saw the overnight rate on a three-month horizon unchanged from one week ago but there were expectations of a rise in more long-term rates, and overnight on a two-year horizon was seen well over seven percent.
The market saw o/n at 6.97 percent in one month, little changed from the 6.94 percent forecast one week ago. On Wednesday, the day Igier based its study, o/n stood at 7.09 percent.
On a three-month timeframe, the implicit o/n rate was seen at 6.79 percent, again very little changed from 6.78 percent seen a week ago. A month ago it was seen at 7.26 percent.
On a one-year horizon, the implicit o/n rate was seen rising to 6.67 percent from 6.59 percent seen a week ago. A month ago it was seen at 7.26 percent.
One a two-year view, the market saw o/n sharply up at 7.17 percent against 6.96 percent seen one week ago. A month ago it was seen at 7.48 percent.

The spread between Italian and German implicit overnight rates on a two-year timeframe, considered a good indicator of market confidence in Italy's early entry into the European economic and monetary union (EMU), was at 245 basis points, out from 228 bps a week ago but in from 267 bps a month ago.
